# Agenda

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Orient students to the arc of the session: equations, diagrams, covariance, implications, lavaan.
:::

# Overview

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Frame LVPA as the combination of the two pieces students already know, not a new method.
:::

## Putting the two parts together

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** State the central idea: LVPA = measurement model (CFA) + structural model (path analysis among latent variables). Same logic as before: theory-driven specification, estimate so the model-implied covariance matches the observed one. Key difference: the structural paths now connect latent variables, not measured ones.
:::

## Review: the structural part (MVPA)

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Reactivate w3 ideas: regressions among measured variables, exogenous/endogenous, disturbances. This is what will now operate on latent variables.
:::

## Review: the measurement part (CFA)

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Reactivate w7 ideas: indicators, loadings, residuals, latent variable as common cause of indicators. This is what defines the latent variables.
:::

## Reframe: research questions

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Show the kind of RQ that needs LVPA (e.g., effect of one construct on another, each measured with multiple indicators), contrasted with MVPA and CFA RQs, as w7 did.
:::

# Systems of equations

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Build the model algebraically first, as in w3 and w7, so diagrams and covariance tracing have something to map onto.
:::

## Measurement equations

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Indicators are written as functions of latent variables (intercept, loading, residual). Unchanged from CFA; reinforce that every latent variable needs its own indicators.
:::

## Structural equations

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Latent variables are written as functions of other latent variables (path coefficient, disturbance). Same form as MVPA regressions, but the variables are latent.
:::

## Combined system

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Put both sets of equations side by side so students see one model with two layers. Introduce the notation distinction (loadings vs. structural paths; residuals vs. disturbances).
:::

# Systems of equations to path diagrams

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Translate the equations into the diagram conventions students already use.
:::

## Path diagram review

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Quick retrieval of symbols: squares, circles, single-headed arrows, curved double-headed arrows.
:::

## Path diagram: structural part

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Show the structural part alone, with latent variables in circles and paths between them.
:::

## Path diagram: measurement part

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Show the measurement part alone, with indicators, loadings and residuals for each latent variable.
:::

## Path diagram: LVPA

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Merge the two diagrams into the full LVPA diagram. Students should be able to point to which arrows belong to which part.
:::

## Exogenous vs. endogenous latent variables

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Extend the w3 exogenous/endogenous distinction to latent variables. Determines which get a variance parameter and which get a disturbance.
:::

## Disturbances vs. residuals

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Prevent confusion between two kinds of error: residuals on indicators (measurement error) and disturbances on endogenous latent variables (unexplained structural variance).
:::

# Model-implied covariance matrix

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Connect specification to estimation: the model implies a covariance matrix among the indicators only, and that is what is compared to the data.
:::

## Review: path tracing rules

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Restate the tracing rules from w3 and w7 so students have them in hand before the new case.
:::

## Tracing through the measurement and structural parts

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Show that implied covariances between indicators of different latent variables run through the loadings and the structural path. Key insight: structure only shows up in the covariance between indicators of different factors.
:::

## Allowed or not allowed?

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Check understanding of valid traces in the combined model (e.g., no going through a collider, no going forward then back).
:::

## Practice

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Students derive implied covariances in a small LVPA on their own, as in the w3 and w7 practice slides.
:::

# Implications

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Spell out what the combined model means for scaling, identification and parameter counting.
:::

## Scale of latent variables

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Each latent variable still needs its scale set (marker loading or fixed variance). Note that endogenous latent variables are scaled via a marker loading, since their variance is not a free parameter.
:::

## Degrees of freedom

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Review how df = information − parameters, with information based on the indicators only. Preview that the structural part can add df.
:::

## Parameters to be estimated

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Count parameters by type (loadings, residual variances, structural paths, disturbance variances, exogenous variances) so students can see where df come from.
:::

## Measurement model first, then structure

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Introduce the logic of checking the CFA before adding structural paths: poor measurement undermines any structural interpretation. Sets up the identification and fit weeks.
:::

# Specifying LVPA models in Lavaan

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Move from diagram to code.
:::

## Lavaan syntax review

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Pull together `=~`, `~`, `~~` and `:=` from w3 and w7 in one table.
:::

## Lavaan syntax: measurement + structural

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Show one model block with a measurement section and a structural section, so students see how each part of the diagram maps to a line of code.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
**Purpose:** Hands-on practice specifying an LVPA in lavaan.
:::
